l At the meeting of Hie West ‘Lanea.shire Rugby Union ' held last Friday. Warrington received thehighest number of votes in the election of Club, to reprtwent the Exocu- : tivc Committee, Widnes eoming next. Both St. Helens l and St. Helens Recreation were elated, but Runcorn was voted on. . There were two changes on the Corn- muter, Birkenhead Wanderers —th” manners of the Junior Cup—and Walkden taking the places of South- port Olyinpie and Litherland.

nie Rochdale Club are considered to love done a good thing, front the point of view of "gate money," in engaging Jack Briggs. The Widnesian is evidently very popular amongst admirers of the summer game, and it to genically concluded that when Briggs is about there will be something worth seeing. It is said that Briggs is put on the Rochdale team every week, and if his important engagements are over in time to admit of his playing he wires to that effect.

To-tlny's cricket matelten ;—Warrington v. Leyland, at Warrington ; Witthen v. Walton, at Walton; Runcorn V. Garston, at Runcorn ; St. Mew V. Stanley. at St. Helens ; St. Helens Recreation V. Prescot, at Pre,tcot.

Runcorn and Frolshant antagonised at the latter place on Saturdav,and the Weal eleven gave the men from Soap- town a tremendous thrashing. The score 1.0 almost sufficient comment :—Frodsham, 128 ; Runcorn, 32. Carpenter gave tile visitors a rare.task of leather hunting in a well compiled 51, and Bettesworth put on the more than respectable scswe of 36. Bettesworth and Jammon made sad havoc with the Runeorn wickets, as the wore indicatee. In the second attempt with the Coat, Runcorn made a better show, scoring 36 for three wickets.

Wt.lnes easily aceounted for Wavertree at Widnes on Satorday, winning by a majority of 92 runs. Woman,' Callon 'lid great execntion with both bat and 1011, and were ably Animated by Thorpe and Oaken. The party of American tourists, who landed in Ireland ' last week, consists, saes a somesrhat cynical serihe, of 28 "noblemen," artists, and ordinary folk, most of whom are riding Quadrant Safeties, purchased on their arrival at Cork. One rider is mounted ono not live American Star Sabity. Ile is certain to be what the story 1100k4 term the cynosure of all eyes." About 35 miles per day will he the average distance accom- plished. It may be done standing up or sitting down. early or late ! The tourists are allowed to choose their own company. They mayß go in twirl or three,, or. in fact, as fancy penults. ut all are requested to be up to scratch at dinner-time, a request that in sure to be complied with in every instance. I doubt, however, whether the same can be said for breakfast.

On saturday the members of the Warrington cycling club had an enjoyable run to Vale Royal. There was a good insister, and the weather was rhartniog. On Tuts- day evening about 25 of the members journeyed on their machines to ssin-ton-le-Willows. I hear that several of tin members propose to snake a tour in North Wales during the Whitsuntide holidays.
